newsitem.title: MEXICO: Gigante to invest 150 mln pesos in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Gigante to invest 150 mln pesos in 1997.

text.p: Grupo Gigante, Mexico's third largest supermarket chain, will invest at least 150 million pesos in store remodelling in 1997 and expects to generate cash flow of 200 million pesos this year, a top official said on Wednesday.
"Investments in 1997 should exceed 150 million pesos which will be put into the remodelling of stores," Gigante deputy finance director Ignacio Toussaint told Reuters.

This year, Gigante staked 50 million pesos of investment into Gigante stores, and also put 200 million pesos into the construction of new Carrefour outlets, which it has built in partnership with the French retailer.
By the end of 1996, Carrefour is expected to have 11 stores in operation in Mexico and 14 by the end of next year.
Toussaint said sales volume was expected to fall an accumulated three percent in 1996 from 1995, but he said the firm was seeking to attract more clients via sales promotions.
"We're seeing growth of 15 percent in the number of clients that visit our stores, that's a good symptom for generating stronger revenues," he said.
In 1997, he expected sales to grow three percent in real terms, and cash flow to increase from 200 million pesos this year to 300 million pesos.

He said the company's debts had dropped from 1.57 billion pesos from 870 million pesos after Inbursa and Banamex took an 18.58 percent stake. Of its existing debts, 225 million pesos is with Banamex and 646 million pesos is with other banks.

Inbursa and Banamex took part in Gigante's one billion peso capitalization. Some 700 million pesos went to paying off debt, 200 million pesos was put into investments in subsidiaries and the rest became working capital.
